title: More protein ≠ more muscle. 🥩
hook: More protein ≠ more muscle. 🥩
caption:
More protein ≠ more muscle. 🥩

You don't need to force-feed yourself 250g of protein just because someone on the internet said so.

For most people who train, 1.6–2.2 g/kg of body weight per day is a solid evidence-based range.

But here's what actually matters:

Eat enough.
Train hard.
Recover properly.
Repeat.

Whether your goal is fat loss, muscle growth or a better physique, consistency will beat extremes every single time.

And no — whey isn't magic. It's simply a convenient way to help you hit your protein target.

title: YOUR PROGRAM SHOULD REMOVE WHAT ISN’T WORKING.
hook: YOUR PROGRAM SHOULD REMOVE WHAT ISN’T WORKING.
caption:
YOUR PROGRAM SHOULD REMOVE WHAT ISN’T WORKING.

A good training program isn’t just about adding more.

Sometimes progress comes from removing what no longer contributes.

If an exercise isn’t helping your goal, a set is creating unnecessary fatigue, or a movement keeps limiting performance, your program should be willing to change.

Look at:

• Exercise effectiveness
• Training volume
• Performance trends
• Technique
• Recovery
• Fatigue
• Progressive overload

Don’t keep an exercise just because it has always been there.

**KEEP WHAT WORKS. REMOVE WHAT DOESN’T. BUILD WHAT PROGRESSES.**

FOMOF
